Basic = diluted (EPS note 11: 'Basic and diluted' 219.23 RMB cents); no dilutive equity instruments -- employee share appreciation rights are cash-settled and already expensed in administrative expenses. Held FLAT; FY2025 buyback of RMB 158.2m (15.0m shares) shows the count is drifting down, not up.

Employee share appreciation rights are cash-settled and sit inside administrative expenses (FY2025 results announcement, 2H2025 admin commentary), so they are already in EBITDA.
inputs.fx_note: Flows and statements in RMB (CNY), AR FY2025 'RMB'000'; SGX quote in SGD. fx_rate 0.1911 SGD per CNY = Yahoo CNYSGD=X at 2026-10-23T21:29Z. Cross check: USDSGD 1.2779 / USDCNY 6.6606 (Yahoo SGD=X, CNY=X, 2026-10-23) = 0.1919, a 0.4% tie that confirms the direction (1 CNY ~ 0.19 SGD; RMB per-share value x 0.1911 = SGD). No dual listing exists for a price parity check; magnitude check: FY2025 EPS RMB 2.192 x 0.1911 = SGD 0.419, P/E 11.6x at SGD 4.88, consistent with SGX consensus-range multiples for the name. Ship contracts are priced in USD and the RMB has appreciated to ~6.66/USD vs ~7.1-7.2 when the 2023-24 orderbook was signed -- that is a flow risk carried in the scenario paths, not in this bridge.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T09:06:50Z SGX regular close (Yahoo chart API regularMarketTime); 52-week range 3.16-5.41
inputs.wacc_rationale: RMB flows, so an RMB rate: China 10y government bond ~1.8-1.9% + beta ~1.2 (cyclical heavy industry) x RMB-market ERP ~6.5% = ~9.6%, rounded to 9.5%. Net cash balance sheet, so WACC = cost of equity. Cyclical, geopolitical (US port-fee / Section 301 measures on China-built ships) and governance risk are charged ONCE, in the scenario paths and the 25/50/25 weights -- no per-scenario WACC and no ad-hoc premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial: lease liabilities nil at FY2025 (AR p.6252), no lease principal paid in FY2025. lease_cost_pct_path 0 and no lease liabilities in net debt -- consistent, nothing omitted.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is RMB 115.9m of RMB 32.26bn equity and the FY2025 NCI profit share was a loss of RMB 5.2m: flows are consolidated and the NCI book value is deducted once in the equity_bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (currency bridge, SBC-zero, matching-asset rule, risk charged once). YZJ is an operating shipbuilder (~94% of FY2025 revenue) plus a 33-vessel dry-bulk fleet (~4%) and minor trading/property. The investment (debt-investment / microfinance) business was spun off as Yangzijiang Financial Holdings in April 2022, so pre-FY2022 EBITDA, interest income and equity are not comparable with today's pure-play; margin anchors use FY2023-FY2025 plus the segment gross margins. EBITDA BASIS: driver margins are OPERATING EBITDA, excluding interest income (RMB 850m, stripped per the net-cash rule) and share of associates/JVs (RMB 861m, whose investments are added at book in the bridge). FY2025 operating EBITDA = 11,322 reported - 850 - 861 = RMB 9,611m = 33.7% of revenue (FY2024 28.1%); shipbuilding gross margin 35% in FY2025 vs 28% FY2024. CYCLE: this is a cyclical peak. Margins are fat because 2023-24 orders were signed at record newbuild prices with low steel costs; FY2025 new orders collapsed to US$2.5bn (vs US$14.6bn FY2024) and the FY2026 target is US$4.5bn. The US$22.4bn orderbook fills capacity to 2H2029, so the paths hold elevated margins through ~2028 and fade to a mid-cycle 15% operating EBITDA margin (shipbuilding GM ~16-17%) by FY2035; revenue in RMB rises with the Hongyuan yard (integrated 2027) then falls back as lower-priced, thinner post-2025 orders replace the peak book. CASH: cash 20,075.7 + restricted cash 6,068.5 (short-term deposits with restricted liquidity before maturity and deposits for borrowings, AR note 13; the 6.07bn was moved out of cash in FY2025 investing) - borrowings 5,500 = net cash RMB 20.6bn. Customer-advance float is NOT all free cash -- see the equity_bridge deduction. WORKING CAPITAL: shipbuilding is prepaid by milestone instalments (net contract liabilities 13,140 - contract assets 5,581 = RMB 7.56bn), so wc_capture is +15% (revenue growth brings in advances, revenue decline returns them); FY2024 contract balances added RMB 7.5bn of OCF and FY2025 reversed 1.1bn, which is why reported FCF fell from 11.9bn to 2.5bn. BUYBACKS: small repurchaser (RMB 158m FY2025); flat count is funded, not a convention. DATA GAP: the H1 FY2026 interim (released 6-Aug-2026) is not in Extracted/. Its headline revenue (RMB 17.5bn, +36%) and net profit (RMB 5.4bn, +28%) are taken from BS6.SI_Analysis.json and set the FY2026 driver year; its balance sheet is not available, so net cash and shares are therefore from the 31-Dec-2025 balance sheet, ~10 months old. Re-anchor when the interim is extracted -- net cash in particular moves by billions with contract balances and the FY2025 final dividend (SGD 0.20/sh, ~RMB 4.1bn, paid ~May 2026), which IS deducted in the equity_bridge. POST-BALANCE-SHEET ITEMS in the bridge: FY2025 final dividend (RMB ~4.1bn) and the premium on the US$825.7m Poseidon stake. Capex for the Jingjiang yard (RMB 3bn, Sep-2026) and LNG terminal (RMB 2bn) is in the FY2026-28 capex path. UNVERIFIED: the Analysis JSON also cites 'US$14.27bn of 2026 YTD order wins across 119 contracts' from press updates; that conflicts with H1 FY2026 wins of US$1.75bn and a flat US$22.4bn orderbook at 30-Jun-2026, so it is NOT used. If confirmed from a company filing it would move the FY2029-32 revenue and margin fade materially upward (toward the bull path).

equity_bridge.item: Investments in joint ventures and associated companies at book
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 AR balance sheet: JVs 1,447.4 + associates 1,097.7 (Jiangsu Yangzi-Mitsui 51% JV, Tsuneishi Zhoushan 34%). Their RMB 861m FY2025 profit share is excluded from operating EBITDA, so the asset comes in here (matching-asset rule). Book, not a multiple of peak earnings -- conservative.
FY2025 AR note 23. Singapore office building and LNG terminal conversion; revenue suspended during renovation, so no income from it is in the flows.

equity_bridge.item: Non-current loans and finance-lease receivables at book
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 AR note 18. Interest earned on these is inside the RMB 850m interest income stripped from the flows.

equity_bridge.item: Excess customer-advance float (net contract liabilities above mid-cycle)
equity_bridge.note: Net contract liabilities RMB 7.56bn at FY2025 (13,140 - 5,581) against ~RMB 1.2-3bn in FY2019-FY2022. Roughly 4.5bn of the net cash pile is peak-cycle customer prepayments that unwind as order intake normalizes (already -1.1bn in FY2025); treated as debt-like rather than free cash.

equity_bridge.item: FY2025 final dividend paid after the balance-sheet date
equity_bridge.note: SGD 0.20/sh x 3,935.6m = SGD 787.1m (FY2025 AR note 33) / 0.1911 = RMB ~4,119m, paid ~May 2026; the current price is ex this dividend, so the cash has left the company. H1 FY2026 operating cash flow is not added because FY2026 is year 1 of the projection.

equity_bridge.item: Poseidon (Seaspan parent) 10% stake: premium paid over independent valuation
equity_bridge.note: US$825.7m paid (completed by Jun-2026, per BS6.SI_Analysis.json) vs Kroll's independent range US$660.6-810.9m (mid 735.8m); the cash left after the 31-Dec-2025 balance sheet but bought an asset, so only the ~US$90m premium over the Kroll mid is value lost: x 6.66 = RMB ~599m. Seaspan dividends are not in the flows; the stake is carried at the Kroll mid through the cash it replaced.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle normalized (base terminal growth). Every trailing CAGR is a peak-cycle or spin-off artefact, so none is a usable forward rate; the base path takes RMB revenue from 28.5bn up to ~33.6bn (FY2028-29) and back to ~29.6bn by FY2035.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 22.3% vs revenue 11.3% (>30% divergence) and vs EPS 45.4%: the equity and EPS series are driven by a margin expansion (operating EBITDA 18.7% FY2022 -> 33.7% FY2025) that is cyclical, not structural. Equity 5yr CAGR is distorted by the April-2022 spin-off of the investment business (equity RMB 35.9bn -> 17.6bn).
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF (OCF - PP&E capex) - interest income (SBC = 0): FY2020 -1,164; FY2021 5,130 (pre-spin-off, interest received 236); FY2022 3,377; FY2023 6,699; FY2024 11,169; FY2025 1,661. The series swings by billions with customer-advance balances, so FCF CAGRs are not meaningful; fcf_5yr_cagr is null because the FY2020 start is negative. EPS in RMB (FY2025 2.192, FY2022 0.713, FY2020 0.644).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +20%: H1 FY2026 revenue was RMB 17.5bn (+36% YoY, per BS6.SI_Analysis.json citing the 6-Aug-2026 interim); an H2 in line with H2 FY2025 (RMB 15.6bn) plus Hongyuan ramp gives ~RMB 34bn. FY2027-28: US$22.4bn orderbook (256 vessels at 30-Jun-2026, deliveries to 2030) plus Hongyuan from 2027, offset by RMB appreciation (USD/CNY ~6.66). FY2029-32: the thin post-peak order intake (US$2.5bn FY2025, US$1.75bn in H1 FY2026, US$4.5bn FY2026 target) replaces the peak book. FY2033+: mid-cycle order run-rate.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY2026 33%: FY2025 operating EBITDA 33.7% and H1 FY2026 net margin 30.9% (RMB 5.4bn / 17.5bn) vs FY2025 30.3% show the peak margin holding through the guidance year. Peak-priced 2023-24 orders deliver through ~2028, then the margin fades to 15% (shipbuilding GM ~16-17%, YZJ's through-cycle level as a top-quartile Chinese yard).
base.capex_rationale: FY2025 capex 7.5% of revenue (PP&E 1,953 + investment property 181). FY2026-28 carry the Hongyuan yard (~RMB 3.0bn), the LNG terminal (~RMB 2.0bn, H1 2027) and the new Jingjiang yard (RMB 3.0bn announced Sep-2026, two-year build): ~RMB 6.7bn over three years in the base path. Then 2.8%, above 2.5% D&A.
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 income tax expense 2,045 on PBT ex associates 9,816 = 20.8%; mix of 25% PRC statutory, 15% high-tech subsidiaries and the Pillar-2 15% floor. Cash paid (1,368) lags the accrual; 20% held flat.

scenario_narratives.base: The contracted orderbook (US$22.4bn, slots filled to 2H2029) delivers as scheduled and Hongyuan lifts volume from 2027, but the RMB's appreciation against USD-priced contracts is a margin headwind from FY2027 (H1 FY2026 margins held at the FY2025 peak), and the order collapse of 2025 (US$2.5bn) and US$1.75bn in H1 FY2026, against a US$4.5bn target, means the post-2029 book is smaller and priced well below the 2023-24 peak. Operating EBITDA margin fades from 33.7% to a 15% mid-cycle; revenue round-trips to ~RMB 29-30bn. The value is roughly half contracted peak cash flows to 2029 and half a mid-cycle shipyard.
scenario_narratives.bull: Fleet-replacement and decarbonisation demand (aging tanker and bulk fleets, dual-fuel container ships, IMO net-zero framework) keeps the upcycle running into the 2030s; YZJ's cost leadership and Hongyuan capacity let it rebuild orders to US$6-8bn a year at prices that hold up, and the mid-cycle margin settles at 20% rather than 15%. Revenue peaks ~RMB 37bn and does not fall back much.
scenario_narratives.bear: The classic shipbuilding bust: excess Chinese yard capacity, US port fees and Section 301 measures on China-built ships pushing Western owners to Korean and Japanese yards, a weak dry-bulk market and continued RMB strength. Order intake stays near FY2025's US$2.5bn, newbuild prices fall, and from 2029 revenue drops ~40% to ~RMB 20bn at a ~10% operating EBITDA margin, close to the FY2016-2021 trough when onerous-contract provisions hit. Customer advances unwind as the book runs off.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the business is at a cyclical margin peak, order intake fell 83% in FY2025, and US trade measures aimed at Chinese-built ships are a live policy risk. Base held at 50%: the contracted orderbook to 2029 makes the near-term path the most predictable part of the valuation. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs both a longer cycle and a structurally higher mid-cycle margin, two independent things going right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a peak-cycle shipbuilder as two pieces: the contracted, peak-priced orderbook cash flows to ~2029 (high confidence on volume, RMB/USD risk on margin) and a mid-cycle shipyard after that, capitalized at a cyclical 12x cap. Net cash is counted net of the peak-cycle customer-advance float, and interest income is stripped so the cash pile is not counted twice. The market price implies peak-ish margins persisting well beyond the orderbook.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin: each 1pp of terminal operating EBITDA margin is worth ~RMB 0.29/share (~SGD 0.06) through the 12x terminal cap; the gap to the price is mostly about how long peak margins last, not the terminal level.
RMB/USD: contracts are USD-priced and costs are RMB; the RMB at ~6.66 vs ~7.2 at signing is a margin headwind that hedging only delays.
Order intake: FY2025 US$2.5bn vs FY2024 US$14.6bn; the FY2026 US$4.5bn target is the first test of the post-peak run-rate.
US port fees / Section 301 measures on China-built vessels and owner diversification to Korean and Japanese yards.

Stale anchors: net cash is from the 31-Dec-2025 balance sheet; the ~RMB 4.1bn FY2025 final dividend is deducted in the bridge, but H1 FY2026 contract-balance movements are not visible until the interim is extracted.
